result:
Review complete — **approved (tier1)**.

The change closes two real, previously-flagged gaps in the DDL authorization gate: it widens keyword coverage to privilege-escalation primitives (GRANT/REVOKE/CREATE ROLE/SECURITY DEFINER/etc.) that previously slipped through, and replaces the shape-only citation check with a real on-disk existence check, so a fabricated-but-well-formed `KE-...` or `OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_...yaml` citation is now correctly rejected. I independently verified (not just trusted the self-report): all 28 tests pass, the module compiles, the YAML parses, and the cited fixture files genuinely exist on disk. The diff doesn't touch `.github/workflows/**` or any tier2-triggering path, consistent with its tier1 classification. Wrote three minor non-blocking nitpicks to `review-verdict.json` (case-sensitive approval marker, existence-without-semantic-relevance, prose false-positives on GRANT/REVOKE) — none are severe enough to reject.
